---
title: "☑️ Best Practices"
subtitle: "Interactive learning for safe EVD management"
---

A quick-reference guide to safe, high-quality care when managing external ventricular drains.

## Do's and Don'ts

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| <span class="mark-do">✔</span> Confirm EVD setting before interpreting ICP | <span class="mark-dont">✖</span> Interpret ICP without knowing the drain setting |
| <span class="mark-do">✔</span> Check clamp status before transport or procedures | <span class="mark-dont">✖</span> Keep EVD closed and not monitor ICP |
| <span class="mark-do">✔</span> Level the transducer at the external auditory meatus | <span class="mark-dont">✖</span> Clamp EVD and leave the transducer at the level of the heart |
| <span class="mark-do">✔</span> Trend ICP and waveform together | <span class="mark-dont">✖</span> Rely on a single ICP value |
| <span class="mark-do">✔</span> Minimize CSF system access | <span class="mark-dont">✖</span> Access CSF unnecessarily |
| <span class="mark-do">✔</span> Use sterile technique for all handling | <span class="mark-dont">✖</span> Break sterility during manipulation |
| <span class="mark-do">✔</span> Secure tubing to prevent dislodgement | <span class="mark-dont">✖</span> Leave tubing unsecured |
| <span class="mark-do">✔</span> Communicate EVD status during handoffs | <span class="mark-dont">✖</span> Assume others know the EVD setup |
| <span class="mark-do">✔</span> Monitor ICP during transport at all times | <span class="mark-dont">✖</span> Transport without considering ICP risk |
| <span class="mark-do">✔</span> Reassess waveform if values seem inconsistent | <span class="mark-dont">✖</span> Ignore dampened or abnormal waveforms |

## CSF Color Interpretation

| CSF Appearance | Clinical Interpretation |
|---|---|
| **Clear** | Normal CSF |
| **Xanthochromia (yellow)** | Suggests prior hemorrhage or SAH breakdown products |
| **Bloody** | May indicate active bleeding, traumatic tap, or evolving hemorrhage |
| **Cloudy** | Concerning for infection (e.g., ventriculitis) |
| **Debris / Particulate** | Possible clot breakdown, infection, or catheter obstruction |

::: {.callout-warning}
**Clinical Note:** Changes in CSF color should always be interpreted in clinical context and may warrant further evaluation.
:::

## Key Takeaway

::: {.callout-tip}
**Clinical Pearl:** Most EVD-related errors are system-based (leveling, clamping, interpretation). A structured approach prevents harm.
:::
